reason: adversarial_review: adversarial reviewer says escalate: plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py's _part_targets git-verb branch (`elif headl == "git" and len(words) >= 2: sub = words[1].lower()`) still reads the subcommand from the fixed position words[1] with no flag-skipping, unlike the cp/mv/rm/tee branches which run _nonflag first. Traced `git -c core.fileMode=false rm CLAUDE.md` by hand: words=['git','-c','core.fileMode=false','rm','CLAUDE.md']; sub becomes '-c', matches none of checkout/restore/rm/mv/apply, so _part_targets yields no candidate and decide() allows a command that genuinely deletes the guardrail file. No token is non-literal, so the fail-closed rule never fires. plugin/ci/settings.ci.json's allow-list already permits bare Bash(git *), so this is reachable in CI, not just by hand.; _inner_shell_command (`if len(words) >= 3 and (words[0].lower(), words[1].lower()) in _INNER_SHELL_PAIRS: return words[2]`) still only recognises the exact adjacent pair. Traced `bash --norc -c 'echo x > CLAUDE.md'`: words=['bash','--norc','-c',...]; ('bash','--norc') is not in _INNER_SHELL_PAIRS, so the quoted inner command is never recursed into; the '>' sits inside the single-quoted outer token so it is correctly treated as literal text at the outer level, not a redirection operator; shell_write_targets returns [] and decide() allows a command that writes the guardrail file via an inner shell.; Both gaps are exactly the class of vulnerability intent.md and spec.md's Design section exist to close (git rm/restore/checkout/apply and bash -c/sh -c recursion are both named as covered idioms with no flag-position qualification); they are not part of plan.md's named residual (unlisted wrappers, pathspec-less git verbs, variable-built paths) -- a leading flag on an already-recognised verb or wrapper is a different, narrower shape that was missed, not weighed and accepted.; No test in tests/test_hooks.py exercises a git invocation with a global option before the subcommand, or an inner-shell call with a flag between the interpreter name and its -c/-Command token: the existing 'git -c user.name=x commit -m y' case belongs to test_plan_sync_detects_commit_in_any_position (a different hook), and test_shell_write_targets_sees_through_wrappers_and_inner_shells only exercises the bare adjacent pairs. The tests therefore pass with both bugs present -- they do not reproduce either bypass.; This is the second review of this exact pair of bugs: the prior HEAD's escalation (08f5e65) already found and described both precisely; fix-requests.json for this round shows empty requests/not_applied, and verifier.md scopes itself explicitly to re-verifying only the unrelated git -C chain-leak fix (commit 3a90bd0), not these two. The devil's-advocate/panel round (commit 7bc5ef2, the only new commit since 08f5e65) upheld 'escalate' as 'park' rather than closing it; no source file changed in that commit. Independently re-tracing both repros against plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py at this HEAD confirms they are unchanged and the bugs are still live.; Blast radius: this is the change's own security control (risk_list item 'auth', status.yaml risk_accepted: [auth]) and the file registered on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase and in CI (plugin/hooks/hooks.json); a gap in the authorization gate itself, reachable through an already allow-listed program (git) with no non-literal token to trip the fail-closed rule, is the exact failure mode intent.md was opened to close, not a cosmetic nit.
